reviews.title: DDR5 Domination
reviews.comment: I built a new gaming PC since my previous one had been having significant issues; it turns out the GPU and CPU were both damaged when moved. In building a new PC I wanted more than I had; stepped up from DDR4 to 5 and from 24GB to 96GB. The performance has been absolutely gorgeous and its stability has been top notch even with my tweaking of specs. They snapped right into my system and I had zero issues running it at base ddr5 clock and then again at its XMP rate. The late 2024/early 2025 price I paid for this was a good value for the money in my mind. Pros: -CL30 is great for gaming (and other tasks) -96GB capacity means I'm almost never straining my system -Discrete design Cons: -With 2025 pricing I'd be unlikely to make this decision for my personal gaming machine -People may dislike Corsair (not sure why personally) Do you need a ton of ram? This might suit you.

reviews.title: Rock solid, worked perfectly.
reviews.comment: I didn't want flashy RGB craziness on my RAM, or any other nonsense to deal with like height issues, so this is the kind of stuff I like to build with. I was a little leery of memory issues since so many people reported them with AM5 installs, but after verifying compatibility with the motherboard before purchase I installed it on a B650 Gigabyte Aorus Elite AX motherboard with a 7800x3D, and had zero problems. It booted right up first try, detected and went through POST faster than I expected, and then set the XMP profile to enabled to run it at 6000 without a hitch (if you buy the AMD labeled version use EXPO, but most motherboards work just fine with either and will detect the timings just fine). Simple, fast, works great with no fuss, can't ask for anything more than that when building a new setup.
